answer.location_description: A small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, at rows 1-3 and columns 1-3. A bright patch there pushes the model toward 'large blob'.
answer.mechanism: Hidden units 1, 7, 11, 12, 14, 16 and 19 detect large blobs: they have positive weights over a broad central disk or annulus. Each also has large positive weights (about +55 to +99) on the 3x3 corner patch. Hidden units 3, 5, 8, 10, 17, 20, 23, 25, 30 and 31 detect small blobs: they have positive weights on the background and centre, negative weights on the ring around the centre, and strongly negative weights (about -30 to -99) on the same patch. So a bright patch excites the large-blob units and suppresses the small-blob units. In layer 2, units u8, u13 and u15 (positive output weights 65, 99, 67) draw positive input from the large-blob units, e.g. u13 gets +87 from unit 7 and u15 gets +97 from unit 11. Units u0, u3, u9 and u12 (output weights -80, -94, -98, -72) draw positive input from the small-blob units, e.g. u3 gets +87 from unit 17 and u9 gets +90 from unit 17. A bright corner patch therefore raises the positive pathways and lowers the negative ones, driving the logit toward class 1.
answer.evidence: In about 17 of 32 hidden units, the only structured weights outside the central blob region sit in rows 1-3, columns 1-3. These magnitudes are among the largest in each unit: unit 1 has 66/59/98, 59/96/71, 70/88/66; unit 16 has 83/99/97; unit 12 has 76-98; unit 3 has -91/-78/-84, -84/-68/-58, -77/-94/-71; unit 31 has -92 to -96. The neighbouring pixels in row 0, row 4 and column 0 show no such pattern. The patch's sign always matches the unit's role: positive in units with a positive central disk or annulus (large-blob units) and negative in units with an inhibitory ring (small-blob units). The layer-2 and output weights then route both sign groups toward a higher class-1 logit.
answer.main_feature: The legitimate size cue is how far the bright blob extends from the centre. Large-blob units respond to brightness over a wide disk or annulus (roughly rows 5-18, cols 5-18), while small-blob units reward a compact bright centre with a dark surrounding ring.
